methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 13 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring
methods.skip_reason: target revenue not on file (private companies rarely disclose)
methods.rationale: Public Semiconductors P/S median is 18.9x across 3 tickers. Cannot apply without target's revenue.

data.narrative:
Groq is a private-stage semiconductor company that has raised $3.54B to date. The target operates within Chips & Semiconductors, a sector populated by 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers including Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, SambaNova Systems, Etched, and Ayar Labs.

Standard triangulation methods yield limited applicability. Peer-median analysis is not viable: while 13 same-sector peers exist, none satisfy narrow stage and valuation-tier filters required for robust median calibration; a threshold of ≥3 filtered datapoints was not met. Public-comp anchoring is similarly constrained by the absence of disclosed revenue figures for Groq. The public semiconductor universe carries a median P/S multiple of 18.9x across the three tickers, but without target revenue data, this multiple cannot be operationalized.

This analysis cannot support a specific valuation range given data constraints. The capital intensity and long development cycles typical of semiconductor manufacturing, combined with Groq's substantial capital raise of $3.54B, suggest a meaningful valuation. However, without revenue disclosure, peer-stage alignment, or other quantifiable operating metrics, conventional analytical methods do not yield defensible output. Material uncertainties include Groq's revenue trajectory, gross margins, and addressable market penetration relative to both public and private semiconductor competitors.
